topic.name: Triple Integrals Over Type III Regions

question.text:
Evaluate the triple integral

\[ \iiint\limits_R 2x \, \textrm{d}V \]

where $R$ is the type III region given by

\[ R= \big\{(x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: x^2 \leq z \leq 2x^2, \: 0 \leq y \leq 2xz \big\}. \]
question.explanation:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

\[ \displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} 2x \: \textrm{d}V = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{2x^2} \int_{0}^{2xz} 2x \: \mathrm{d}y \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x. \]

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{2x^2} \int_{0}^{2xz} 2x \: \mathrm{d}y \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{2x^2} \left[ \int_{0}^{2xz} 2x \: \mathrm{d}y \right] \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{2x^2} 2x \big[ y \big]_{y=0}^{y=2xz} \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{2x^2} 2x(2xz) \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{2x^2} 4x^2z \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \end{align*}

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant:

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{2x^2} 4x^2z \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{1} \left[ \int_{x^2}^{2x^2} 4x^2z \: \mathrm{d}z \right] \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 2x^2 \big[ z^2 \big]_{z=x^2}^{z=2x^2} \: \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 2x^2 \left( (2x^2)^2 - (x^2)^2 \right) \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 6x^6 \: \mathrm{d}x \end{align*}

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x{:}$

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} 6x^6 \: \mathrm{d}x &= \left[ \dfrac{6x^7}{7} \right]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{6}{7}. \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type III Region

question.text:
Evaluate the triple integral $ \displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 12xz \: \mathrm{d}V $ over the region $R,$ shown above.

Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.
question.explanation:
Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 4-x-z \big\}, \]

where

\[ D = \big\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 2 \big\} \]

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 4-x-z \big\} \]

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

\[ \displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} 12xz \: \textrm{d}V = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} \int_{0}^{4-x-z} 12xz \: \mathrm{d}y \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x. \]

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} \int_{0}^{4-x-z} 12xz \: \mathrm{d}y \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} \left[ \int_{0}^{4-x-z} 12xz \: \mathrm{d}y \right] \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} 12xz \big[ y \big]_{y=0}^{y=4-x-z} \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} 12xz(4-x-z) \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} (48xz-12x^2z-12xz^2) \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x \end{align*}

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant:

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{2} (48xz-12x^2z-12xz^2) \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{1} \left[ \int_{0}^{2} (48xz-12x^2z-12xz^2) \: \mathrm{d}z \right] \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \big[ 24xz^2-6x^2z^2-4xz^3 \big]_{z=0}^{z=2} \: \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} (64x - 24x^2) \: \mathrm{d}x \end{align*}

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x{:}$

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} (64x - 24x^2) \: \mathrm{d}x &= \left[ 32x^2 - 8x^3 \right]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\[5pt] &= \left(32-8\right) - 0 \\[5pt] &= 24. \end{align*}

example.title: Constructing and Evaluating Triple Integrals Over Type III Regions From Diagrams

question.text: Evaluate the mixed integral \[ \displaystyle \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{1-x^2}} 6y \,\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}A \] given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by \[ D = \big\{ (x,z) \, : \, 0 \leq z \leq 1-x, \: 0 \leq x \leq 1 \big\}. \]
question.explanation:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $z$ and $x$ as constants:

\begin{align} \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{1-x^2}} 6y \,\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}A &= \iint\limits_D \big[ 3y^2 \big]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{1-x^2}} \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D 3(1-x^2) \: \textrm{d}A \end{align}

Notice that $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane. Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x{:}$

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_D 3(1-x^2) \: \textrm{d}A &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-x} 3(1-x^2) \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 3(1-x^2) \left[ \int_{0}^{1-x} \: \textrm{d}z \right] \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 3(1-x^2) \left[ z \right]_{z=0}^{z=1-x} \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 3(1-x^2)(1-x) \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 3(1-x-x^2+x^3) \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 3\left[ x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2 - \dfrac{1}{3}x^3+ \dfrac{1}{4}x^4 \right]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\[5pt] &=3 \left( 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}+ \dfrac{1}{4} \right) - 0 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{4} \end{align*}

topic.name: Triple Integrals Over Type III Regions

question.text:
Evaluate the triple integral

\[ \displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 4x \: \mathrm{d}V \]

where the region $R$ is given by \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \: x^2 \leq y \leq 1 \right\}, \] and $D$ is a finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the $z$-axis, and the curve $ z + x^2 = 1$ in the first quadrant.
question.explanation:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

\[ \displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} 4x \, \textrm{d}V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{x^2}^{1} 4x \, \mathrm{d}y \right] \mathrm{d}A. \]

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{x^2}^{1} 4x \, \mathrm{d}y \right] \mathrm{d}A &= \iint\limits_{D} 4x \big[ y \big]_{y=x^2}^{y=1} \, \mathrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_{D} 4x(1-x^2) \: \mathrm{d}A \end{align*}

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane shown below.

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_{D} 4x(1-x^2) \, \mathrm{d}A &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-x^2} 4x(1-x^2) \, \mathrm{d}z \, \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 4x(1-x^2) \left[ \int_{0}^{1-x^2} 1 \, \mathrm{d}z \right] \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 4x(1-x^2) \big[ z \big]_{z=0}^{z=1-x^2} \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 4x(1-x^2) (1-x^2-0) \, \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} 4x(1-x^2)^2 \, \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= -2\int_{0}^{1} (-2x)(1-x^2)^2 \, \mathrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= -2\left[\dfrac{(1-x^2)^3}3\right]_{0}^{1} \\[5pt] &= -2\left(0-\dfrac{1}3\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac23 \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type III Region

question.text: Given that $R$ is the type III region shown above, $ \displaystyle \iiint\limits_R x^2 \: \textrm{d}V = $
question.explanation:
For a type III region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \,\textrm{d}V = \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} f(x,y,z) \,\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}A. \]

We consider the region $R$ as a type III region enclosed between the back surface $y = u_1(x,z) = 2$ and the front surface $y = u_2(x,z) = 6.$

So, the region $R$ is given by

\[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \: 2 \le y \le 6 \right\}. \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane with the upper curve

\[ z =1-x. \]

Hence, $D = \left\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \le x \le 1, \: 0 \le z \le 1-x \right\}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows: \begin{align*} \iiint\limits_R x^2 \,\textrm{d}V &= \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{2}^{6} x^2 \,\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-x} \left[ \int_{2}^{6} x^2 \,\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-x} x^2 \big[ y \big]_{y=2}^{y=6} \,\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-x} 4x^2 \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \end{align*}
